edit.description: the rendered result line reads the `AgentUsage` the same walk already lifted, instead of re-reading the event's own keys
the line and the reported usage read against one decode

summary: `formatResult` and `extractResultUsage` each decode the same six provider keys off the same `result` event, and only one of them keeps absence absent

per.section: Derived state is computed, never restated beside its source

acceptance: one decode of a `result` event answers both the usage the invocation reports and the line the renderer prints, so a provider key the event stops carrying cannot leave one side honest and the other confident
pins: a rendered result line reports the same turn, token and cost figures the invocation's usage reports
notes: Verified this tick: `emitLine` (`src/Agent.ts:557`) calls `extractResultUsage` and, through `:666`, `formatResult` (`:753`) on one event; both read `usage.input_tokens`, `usage.output_tokens`, `num_turns`, `duration_ms`, `total_cost_usd`. `:549` claims the walk is shared; the decode is not. `num` (`:768`) coerces absent to `0`, the distinction `AgentUsage` (`:112`) keeps, so the two disagree about absence by construction.
